rule: Allow current Node assert candidates in the four Codex cleanup tests only when they verify machine sentinels, parser fixtures, shipped-copy equality, runtime behavior, or security boundaries without pinning authored prose, headings, tone, or status wording.

allowed.rationale: Verifies that the auto-update command entered the started state; the boolean is observable control-flow state and does not constrain notice wording.
Verifies the spawned update command completed with exit status zero, an executable runtime result independent of generated notice copy.
Verifies one notice is emitted in both the successful-update and marketplace-flow branches; the duplicated occurrence checks result cardinality without pinning either notice's prose.
Checks propagation of the structured fromVersion and toVersion state into the update result while leaving all surrounding notice wording unrestricted.
Uses a synthetic sentinel to prove the LazyCodex release-note section parser retains selected fixture data; no authored release-note sentence is required.
Uses a synthetic sentinel to prove release-note data outside the selected section is filtered out, without constraining editorial release-note content.
Pins the opening lazycodex_release_notes tag because downstream trust-boundary parsing consumes that structured delimiter, not because of presentation wording.
Requires exactly one opening trust-boundary tag so untrusted release-note data cannot create ambiguous nested regions.
Pins the closing lazycodex_release_notes tag as the machine-recognized terminator for the untrusted release-note region.
Requires exactly one closing trust-boundary tag so injected fixture delimiters cannot terminate or duplicate the protected region.
Verifies an injected closing tag is HTML-escaped and remains inert data inside the release-note boundary.
Verifies an injected opening tag is HTML-escaped rather than becoming a nested machine delimiter.
Uses the structured opening and closing tags to extract only the bounded untrusted payload; the regex defines the trust boundary rather than user-facing prose.
The derived candidate repeats the same structured extraction regex while checking that a bounded payload was produced; it contracts delimiters, not authored text.
Checks that structured tag extraction produced a string payload before inspecting it, without imposing payload wording.
Uses a synthetic untrusted-data sentinel to prove hostile fixture content remains present inside the bounded payload instead of being interpreted or moved outside it.
Verifies marketplace-managed installs do not start the self-update command when version lookup times out; this is fail-closed dispatch state.
marketplace-flow is the structured reason code returned by auto-update dispatch and consumed as state, not authored notice wording.
Checks presence of a string notice in the marketplace-flow result while deliberately leaving its status wording unrestricted.
Verifies each dynamically selected input evidence field is reflected into the generated body; the assertion follows fixture values and does not pin headings or fixed prose.
Verifies every dynamic verification-command fixture is emitted by the body serializer without requiring a Verification heading or surrounding authored copy.
Pins the lazycodex-generated tag as a machine label used to identify generated PR bodies, not as editorial PR-body prose.
Verifies the PR-body CLI exits successfully after reading JSON and writing the requested output file.
Compares CLI-written bytes with the exported production formatter for the same dynamic input, so editorial rewrites remain allowed while CLI and library output must stay identical.
Verifies exactly one ulw-loop UserPromptSubmit handler is dispatched for the aggregate plugin, independent of hook status copy.
Verifies exactly one dedicated ultrawork UserPromptSubmit handler is dispatched, preserving routing and deduplication without testing UI wording.
Checks only the structured OmO version prefix and non-empty suffix after installation; the actual user-visible status wording remains free to change.
Verifies the installer removed the stale source version from each status field during version-stamp transformation without constraining the remaining status text.
